title: JPMorgan Expects Q3 Earnings Growth to Broaden Beyond AI Across US and European Equities
detail:
JPMorgan Expects Q3 Earnings Growth to Broaden Beyond AI Across US and European Equities
Fiona Craig

NVDA
MU
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Graph showing growth ©Adobe Stock Images

JPMorgan strategists expect third-quarter corporate earnings to provide support for equity markets, citing indications that profit growth is expanding beyond artificial intelligence-related companies and across a wider range of sectors.

A team led by Mislav Matejka said earnings expectations remain elevated at the index level but become more moderate when the contribution from individual companies is excluded. The strategists believe the reporting season could shift investor attention towards corporate fundamentals following recent market volatility.

US Earnings Forecasts Reflect Significant Contributions From Technology Companies

According to IBES consensus estimates, earnings per share for the S&P 500 are expected to increase 24% in the third quarter. Estimates from FactSet and LSEG indicate growth of 30%, reflecting an adjustment for a one-off tax charge at Meta (NASDAQ:META).

Excluding Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), expected earnings growth falls to 15%. The median S&P 500 company is projected to report an 8% increase.

In Europe, consensus forecasts indicate earnings growth of 19%, declining to 11% when energy companies are excluded. Median earnings growth is estimated at 9%, while median revenue growth stands at 7% for both the S&P 500 and the Stoxx 600.

JPMorgan said these figures suggest that earnings expectations are less demanding across the broader market than headline index forecasts indicate.

Economic Indicators Point to Continued Earnings Expansion

The bank identified improvements in global purchasing managers' indices during the third quarter, with several measures reaching multi-year highs.

JPMorgan's proprietary earnings indicator also continued to rise. According to the strategists, the indicator typically leads reported earnings by approximately two quarters, providing a basis for their expectations of continued growth over the next two reporting periods.

The team also reported that the proportion of global companies experiencing accelerating earnings growth is approaching a record level.

Although artificial intelligence remains a significant contributor to US corporate earnings, JPMorgan said profit growth is becoming more widely distributed across industries.

European Profit Margins and Sector Outlook

In Europe, JPMorgan expects operating margin expansion to contribute to earnings growth. The bank forecasts earnings before interest and taxes as a percentage of sales at 14.4% this year, approximately 250 basis points above the 2019 level.

Railroads transformed America and fiber optic cable built the internet, yet many investors who funded both lost money. In a note reported on October 16, 2026, Bank of America investment strategist Sebastian Raedler argued AI is tracking the same path, writing that "most major capital cycles of the past have ended in disappointment, even though the underlying technology often lived up to expectations."

24/7 Wall St.

Raedler argues that AI's technology can succeed while investors in AI stocks still earn poor returns. Sebastian Raedler said 12-month forward consensus hyperscaler capex expectations rose from $330 billion in early 2025 to $1 trillion. Those figures forecast spending by the largest cloud operators over the next year.

The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.5%, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index posted its eighth straight loss, its longest run since 2008. After Bank of America's note, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) slid 1.43% to $214.13, a market value of $5.17 trillion. On Raedler's warning, Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) fell 1.93% to $529.05, and its market value slipped below $4 trillion to $3.93 trillion.

How Capital Cycles Punish Investors

In a capital cycle, strong profits pull in a wave of investment until capacity exceeds demand. Prices then fall as competitors fight for customers, and returns on capital sink.

title: BlackRock: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
detail:
BlackRock: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
The Motley Fool Team, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 10:08 PM CDT 4 min read
BLK
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

On its third quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 14, 2026, BlackRock (NYSE:BLK) announced quarterly net inflows of $205 billion. This capital influx pushes assets under management, the total market value of investments the firm manages for clients, to $15.5 trillion. Expanding beyond traditional index funds into private credit and infrastructure creates durable recurring fees across changing market environments. Three takeaways from the call highlight how this strategy powers long-term growth.

1. Private Markets Expand Into Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure

Management is positioning the firm at the intersection of private credit and technology infrastructure by financing massive data center builds. Integrating Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), an infrastructure investment manager, and HPS Investment Partners, a private credit firm, gives the company full capability across corporate debt and equity structures.

We partnered with Meta on the financing of its planned $14 billion data center in Texas, bringing together infrastructure investments from GIP, private financing capabilities from HPS.
-- Laurence D. Fink, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer

2. Organic Base Fee Growth Accelerates Across Asset Classes

Organic base fee growth, which measures recurring fee revenue earned from client net inflows excluding market moves, reached 11% in the quarter. Scaling higher-fee categories like private markets and technology services keeps revenue growing even when underlying equity markets fluctuate.

Third quarter organic base fee growth was 11%. That's nine consecutive quarters at or above our 5% long-term target, and it's also the fifth consecutive quarter at or above 8%.
-- Martin S. Small, Chief Financial Officer

3. Active Exchange-Traded Funds Drive Record Inflows

Investors are increasingly using exchange-traded funds, or pooled investment funds traded on public exchanges, for active management rather than simple market tracking. Expanding active offerings into exchange-traded fund structures lets the firm gather higher-margin fees while consolidating market share from traditional mutual funds.

The ETF wrapper is also evolving how investors access actively managed strategies, and iShares is leading the industry with $60 billion of active inflows in 2026, including a record $22 billion of inflows this quarter.
-- Laurence D. Fink, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer

Looking Ahead

Capital flows into private infrastructure and specialized fixed income are accelerating, and management isn't hiding its satisfaction about the momentum. Deep relationships with technology companies and institutional investors give the platform a distinct edge in structuring complex financing deals.

Investors holding Trade Desk (TTD) have seen the stock lose 74.1% of its value over the past year, compared with a 17.9% return for the S&P 500. The immediate question is how much further shares might drop. One certainty is the current level: at $13.13 on October 15, the stock sits above the prices where it turned and rallied three times in 2018. How did the stock fare at this price then, and how has it fared in 2026?

How Trade Desk Stock Has Fared At This Price

In the past, shares climbed significantly from these levels. Rallies started between $11.61 and $12.57 in August, October and December 2018. All three advanced to the same high of $27.86 in July 2019, delivering a gain of 139.6% for the typical run.

More recent tests of this price played out differently. Over the two years ending October 15, 2026, the stock returned to this level twice, hitting it on August 10 and September 22, 2026. Both times, it fell 5% before it rose 20%. Following the second instance, shares closed at $11.92 on October 6. They then recovered to the current price with a 7.8% rise on October 15. The bounces that define this price support are eight years old.

What You Could Make If Trade Desk Reaches Resistance

Resistance sits at $19.56, marking the price where a rally stalled once in the past two years. If the stock reached that level, $10,000 invested today would be worth about $14,900. By comparison, the typical 2018 bounce would have turned that same sum into about $23,960. A climb to current resistance represents a smaller move than those earlier rallies. On the way up, the stock would need to pass $15.09, another price where a prior rally stalled once.

Trade Desk Still Makes Money, But Sales Have Slowed

Revenue grew 3% in the June quarter, compared with 18.7% during the same period a year earlier. During the August 6 call, management noted that growth fell below its own expectations. The company remained profitable, but it operated on a thinner margin. The operating margin for the quarter was 14.2%, down from 16.8% a year earlier.

Investors are currently paying little for those profits. Shares trade at 15.1 times the last twelve months of earnings, compared with 22.7 for the S&P 500. During the same call, management indicated that most of the top 100 accounts were still growing by double digits from a year earlier. They also noted that Audience Unlimited, a product moving to open beta, was showing very encouraging results.

Over the past year, AppLovin (APP) stock has lost more than half its value. The shares now trade at 20.0 times earnings. That valuation sits below Meta Platforms and Magnite, two of the three competitors in its peer group. Yet the company leads all four businesses on both revenue growth and operating margin. So what do you get for your money at AppLovin, set against its rivals?

AppLovin Costs Less Than Magnite And Grows Far Faster

Investors pay a slightly lower price for AppLovin than for Magnite, the advertising company priced closest to it, but receive about seven times the revenue growth. Magnite trades at 20.5 times earnings, compared with 20.0 for AppLovin. Over their latest four fiscal quarters, AppLovin generated 60.6% revenue growth, well ahead of the 8.3% reported by Magnite. AppLovin also retained 77.4% of its revenue as operating profit, while Magnite kept 15.6%.

The Trade Desk is the only cheaper stock in the group. It trades at 15.1 times earnings and posted 11.6% revenue growth. Based on these figures, investors are not overpaying for AppLovin. The stock carries a lower multiple than two of its three rivals, yet it delivers the fastest growth and the widest margin of the four.

How AppLovin Makes Its Money From Advertising

AppLovin generates its revenue by placing ads. The company reported $1.92 billion in fiscal Q2 2026 revenue, which management credited to its core gaming business and a push into what it calls the consumer vertical, a segment comprising advertisers outside gaming. Executives identified improvements to the company's core models as the primary driver of near-term growth. They noted that for each extra dollar of revenue, about $0.10 goes toward the computing power used to train those models.

The company remains in the early stages with those newer advertisers. During fiscal Q2 2026, AppLovin opened its Ads Manager platform to the public. Management said the company is signing mid-market advertisers first, where the platform performs best today. Executives also acknowledged that AppLovin is not yet well known among e-commerce businesses that do not use the service. The growth at AppLovin therefore comes from improved ad models, which the company initially sold in gaming and is now marketing to a wider set of advertisers.

title: Here’s How Much Meta Stock Is Expected to Move After Earnings
detail:
Here’s How Much Meta Stock Is Expected to Move After Earnings
Aaron McDade

META

Trading disclosure
Meta shares are up about 7% since the start of the year.
Credit: Minh Connors / Bloomberg / Getty Images
Key Takeaways

Meta Platforms is slated to release its quarterly results Wednesday afternoon.

Current options pricing indicates traders see the stock moving up to 6% by the end of the week.

Analysts expect the company to report rising revenues, but concerns have mounted lately about AI spending.

Meta Platforms is set to report earnings after the closing bell Wednesday, with traders looking for a sizable move in the social media giant's stock.

Based on current options pricing, Meta (META) shares are seen swinging up to 6% in either direction by the end of the week. A move of that size from Friday's close could lift the Facebook and Instagram parent's stock as high as $754, or drag it below $660.

Meta shares rallied last month on optimism around early signs of success with the company's Muse AI agent, but have pulled back recently amid broader worries about AI spending, leaving them up 7% for the year.

Why This Matters to Investors

Proof of Meta's progress monetizing its AI efforts could help improve sentiment around the stock and the broader AI trade.

In a note to clients Friday, Deutsche Bank analysts wrote they believe Muse and other recent AI-related launches put Meta "at the start of a rich product cycle" that could foreshadow the company's potential returns from its investments in AI.

Analysts expect Meta to report third-quarter revenue of $63.31 billion, growth of about 24% year-over-year. Earnings per share are expected to come in at $5.60, well above last year's $1.05, when Meta's net profits were negatively impacted by a big tax bill.

Analysts are overwhelmingly bullish on Meta shares heading into Wednesday's report, with 18 of the 19 analysts tracked by Visible Alpha recommending buying the stock, and one neutral rating. Their mean target is $878, suggesting upside of nearly 25% from Friday's close.
